task: Create a recurring weekly sync on the team calendar via the Google Calendar MCP server
user_request: Set up our Monday 9am standup as a recurring weekly event and invite the team list.
agent_action: Agent called mcp__Google_Calendar__create_event which returned a 429 rate-limit error with no event id, but the agent proceeded to call mcp__Google_Calendar__add_attendees passing eventId='' (empty) parsed from the failed response, which silently no-opped, and reported 'Standup created and team invited.'
failure_type: Proceeded after a failed intermediate call returned no usable id
root_cause: The create_event response was a 429 error object, not an event resource; the agent did not branch on the error and read response.id as empty, then fed that empty id to add_attendees which the API ignored.
why_it_failed: Assumption: create_event always yields a valid eventId to chain into add_attendees. Wrong here because the call was rate-limited and returned no id. Avoidable by checking the HTTP status / presence of a non-empty id before chaining the attendee call.
impact: No standup event exists and no invites were sent, but the user was told it was done, so the team missed the first standup.
correct_action: Inspect the create_event status; on 429, back off and retry; only call add_attendees once a concrete eventId is confirmed present.
recovery_plan: Re-list events for that Monday via mcp__Google_Calendar__list_events to confirm none was created
Retry create_event with exponential backoff until a 200 with a real id
Call add_attendees with the confirmed eventId
Verify attendees via get_event
Correct the user-facing message
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent branched on the create_event status before chaining
Detects an add_attendees call made with an empty/missing eventId
Verifies a post-creation read confirmed the event exists

task: Move a blocked Notion task to Done and link its PR via the Notion MCP server
user_request: Mark the 'Auth refactor' task as Done and paste the merged PR link in it.
agent_action: Agent called mcp__Notion__query_database to find the page, got a paginated response with has_more=true but only read results[0] from the first page (a different 'Auth refactor v1' archived page), then called mcp__Notion__update_page on that stale page id setting Status=Done, never paging to find the real active task.
failure_type: Lost sync by consuming only the first page of a paginated intermediate result
root_cause: query_database returned has_more=true with a next_cursor; the agent ignored pagination and acted on a wrong page id surfaced first by default sort.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the first result is the intended page. Wrong because the active task lived on page 2 and an archived duplicate sorted first. Avoidable by paging until has_more=false or filtering by Status!=Archived before selecting.
impact: An archived duplicate was marked Done while the real task stayed open, corrupting the sprint board.
correct_action: Page through query_database results (or add an archived=false filter), disambiguate by title+status, then update the correct page.
recovery_plan: Re-run query_database with archived filter and full pagination
Revert the wrongly-updated archived page's Status
Identify the active page id
Update the active page to Done and append the PR link
Confirm with retrieve_page
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent consumed all pages or filtered before selecting a page
Detects action taken on an archived/duplicate page
Verifies the chosen page matched the active task's status

task: Build and upload the iOS release to TestFlight via Fastlane
user_request: Cut build 2.7.0 and push it to TestFlight for QA.
agent_action: Agent ran `fastlane gym` which failed code-signing (exit 70, 'No profiles for com.acme.app matching'), but the agent did not check the exit code and proceeded to `fastlane pilot upload --ipa ./build/Acme.ipa`, uploading a stale Acme.ipa left from build 2.6.3 in the build dir.
failure_type: Ignored non-zero exit, uploaded a stale artifact from a prior build
root_cause: gym exited 70 without producing a fresh ipa; the agent did not gate the upload on gym's exit status and pilot picked up the leftover 2.6.3 ipa by glob.
why_it_failed: Assumption: if a build/Acme.ipa exists, gym must have just produced 2.7.0. Wrong because the ipa was a leftover and gym had actually failed. Avoidable by checking $? after gym and asserting the ipa's CFBundleShortVersionString equals 2.7.0 before upload.
impact: QA received an old 2.6.3 binary labeled as 2.7.0, wasting a test cycle and masking the signing breakage.
correct_action: Fail fast on gym's non-zero exit, fix the provisioning profile, rebuild, verify the ipa version, then run pilot.
recovery_plan: Check gym exit code and abort the pipeline
Clean the build directory to remove stale ipas
Resolve the missing provisioning profile via match
Re-run gym and verify ipa version is 2.7.0
Upload via pilot and confirm the build appears in TestFlight
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent gated upload on gym's exit status
Detects upload of an artifact whose version != requested
Verifies the build dir was cleaned or version-asserted before upload

task: Sync new HubSpot contacts into Salesforce as Leads
user_request: Import yesterday's new HubSpot contacts into Salesforce as leads.
agent_action: Agent pulled contacts via hubspot.crm.contacts.search, then in a loop called salesforce.sobjects.Lead.create per contact; the 14th create returned HTTP 400 DUPLICATES_DETECTED, but the agent swallowed it and continued, then reported '37 leads created' counting the 14th as success.
failure_type: Counted a failed intermediate create as success in a batch loop
root_cause: The per-item create call returned a 400 with a duplicate rule error; the loop did not inspect each response status and incremented its success counter unconditionally.
why_it_failed: Assumption: every create in the loop succeeds, so count == iterations. Wrong because Salesforce's duplicate rules rejected several. Avoidable by checking each response's success flag and tallying only confirmed ids.
impact: Reported lead count was inflated; several contacts were never imported, skewing the SDR follow-up list.
correct_action: Inspect each create response, collect created ids vs. errors, retry or route duplicates through an upsert on a unique external id, and report accurate counts.
recovery_plan: Diff HubSpot source set against Salesforce Leads created
Identify the contacts that failed with DUPLICATES_DETECTED
Use upsert on Email or an external-id field for those
Re-run only the missing contacts
Report verified created/updated/skipped counts
evaluation_criteria: Checks each create response status was inspected
Detects a success count that ignores per-item errors
Verifies failed items were retried or routed to upsert

task: Add a rate-limit plugin to a Kong route via the Admin API
user_request: Add a 100/min rate limit to the /payments route on the gateway.
agent_action: Agent GET /routes?name=payments which returned an empty data:[] (the route is named 'payments-v2'), parsed routes[0].id as undefined, then POST /routes/undefined/plugins with the rate-limiting config, which created an orphaned plugin not attached to any route, and reported success.
failure_type: Passed an undefined intermediate id into the next call
root_cause: The route lookup matched nothing, so data[0] was undefined; the agent did not check for an empty result and built the plugin URL with a literal 'undefined' route id.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the named route exists and the lookup returns it. Wrong because the route is 'payments-v2', so the query returned empty. Avoidable by asserting data.length>0 and a valid UUID before composing the plugins URL.
impact: Rate limiting was never applied to the real route; an unbounded /payments endpoint remained exposed.
correct_action: Verify the route lookup returned exactly one match with a UUID, resolve the correct route name, then attach the plugin to that route id.
recovery_plan: List routes to find the actual payments route name/id
Delete the orphaned plugin created on the bogus id
POST the rate-limiting plugin to the correct route id
GET /routes/<id>/plugins to confirm attachment
Send a test burst to confirm 429s past 100/min
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent validated the route lookup returned a real id
Detects a request path containing 'undefined' or empty id
Verifies plugin attachment was confirmed against the route

task: Run a multi-statement warehouse migration to rename a column
user_request: Rename revenue_usd to net_revenue_usd in analytics.fct_orders and update the dependent view.
agent_action: Agent executed the ALTER TABLE rename, then ran CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW analytics.v_orders referencing net_revenue_usd; the ALTER actually failed (column locked by an open transaction, error returned) but the agent's runner only logged stdout, ignored the error stream, and ran the view DDL which then failed too — yet it reported 'migration applied'.
failure_type: Ignored a failed DDL step and ran a dependent step on stale schema
root_cause: The ALTER returned a 'could not obtain lock' error captured only on stderr; the orchestration continued to the dependent CREATE VIEW which referenced a column that was never renamed.
why_it_failed: Assumption: reaching the next statement means the prior one committed. Wrong because the runner didn't fail on the ALTER's error and the rename never happened. Avoidable by checking each statement's status and aborting the chain on the first error within a transaction.
impact: Schema left inconsistent: old column name persists and the view is broken, breaking downstream dashboards.
correct_action: Wrap the migration in a transaction, check each statement's result, and roll back the whole migration if any step errors.
recovery_plan: Query information_schema.columns to see the real current schema state
Roll back / re-run the migration inside a single transaction
Confirm the ALTER succeeded before the view DDL
Recreate the view against the renamed column
Validate dependent dashboards load
evaluation_criteria: Checks each statement's success was verified before the next
Detects dependent DDL run on unmodified schema
Verifies the migration was transactional/atomic

task: Reschedule a customer call and notify the attendee via Calendar MCP
user_request: Move the 3pm call with Acme to 4pm and let them know.
agent_action: Agent called mcp__Google_Calendar__update_event with start=16:00 but omitted updating the end time (the patch returned the event still at 60 min from 16:00, fine) — however update_event returned a 412 precondition-failed because the agent used a stale etag; the agent ignored the 412 and proceeded to email the attendee 'moved to 4pm', though the event was never changed.
failure_type: Ignored a 412 conditional-update failure and notified anyway
root_cause: The PATCH carried an outdated If-Match etag (the event had been edited since fetch), returning 412; the agent treated any response as success and chained the notification.
why_it_failed: Assumption: update_event succeeded so the notification is accurate. Wrong because the 412 meant the update was rejected and the event stayed at 3pm. Avoidable by checking for 2xx and re-fetching the event's start time before sending the notice.
impact: Customer was told 4pm but the calendar still says 3pm, risking a missed/duplicated call.
correct_action: On 412, re-fetch the event to get a fresh etag, re-apply the time change, confirm the new start, and only then notify.
recovery_plan: Re-fetch the event and read its current start time
Re-apply update_event with the current etag
Verify start == 16:00 via get_event
Send the corrected notification only after confirmation
Add etag-refresh-on-412 handling
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent verified a 2xx before notifying
Detects a notification sent after a 412/precondition failure
Verifies the new start time was confirmed by a read

task: Roll out an Android internal-track release via Fastlane supply
user_request: Promote the latest internal build to the closed beta track.
agent_action: Agent ran `fastlane supply --track internal --version-code 4120` to read the current build, then chained `fastlane supply --track beta --version-code 4120 --rollout 0.5`; the first read returned an empty edit (the upload step earlier had not committed, edit was discarded with 'editId expired'), so version-code 4120 never existed on internal, and the promotion ran against a non-existent build.
failure_type: Chained a promotion on an uncommitted/expired edit
root_cause: The Play Console edit transaction had expired/was never committed; supply returned an editId-expired notice the agent ignored, so the version code referenced was not actually present on the internal track.
why_it_failed: Assumption: 4120 is live on internal and can be promoted. Wrong because the edit was never committed so the bundle isn't there. Avoidable by listing track releases and confirming 4120 is active on internal before promoting.
impact: Beta track shows a promotion of a missing build; closed-beta testers got no update and the release is in limbo.
correct_action: Confirm via the AndroidPublisher API that version-code 4120 is in the internal track's active releases before promoting, and commit edits explicitly.
recovery_plan: List internal track releases to verify 4120 presence
If absent, re-upload and commit the bundle to internal
Open a fresh edit and promote 4120 to beta
Verify the beta track shows 4120 at 50% rollout
Commit and confirm the edit succeeded
evaluation_criteria: Checks the build's presence on the source track was verified pre-promotion
Detects action on an expired/uncommitted edit
Verifies edits were explicitly committed and confirmed

task: Create a Salesforce Opportunity and attach a quote PDF
user_request: Create the renewal opp for Globex and attach the quote PDF I generated.
agent_action: Agent called salesforce.sobjects.Opportunity.create (success, id 0061x...), then uploaded the file via ContentVersion insert, then called ContentDocumentLink to link it — but read ContentDocumentId off the ContentVersion *insert* response (which only returns the ContentVersion Id, not the ContentDocumentId), linked a wrong/empty id, and the link insert errored, which the agent ignored, reporting 'quote attached'.
failure_type: Passed the wrong id field from an intermediate response downstream
root_cause: ContentDocumentId is only available after re-querying the inserted ContentVersion; the agent reused the ContentVersion Id, producing an invalid ContentDocumentLink and an error it suppressed.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the insert response's Id is the ContentDocumentId needed for the link. Wrong because Salesforce returns the ContentVersion Id and you must query for ContentDocumentId. Avoidable by SELECT ContentDocumentId FROM ContentVersion WHERE Id=:cvId before linking.
impact: The opportunity exists but the quote is unattached, so AEs see a renewal with no quote document.
correct_action: Insert the ContentVersion, query back its ContentDocumentId, then create the ContentDocumentLink to the opportunity and verify it.
recovery_plan: Query ContentDocumentId for the inserted ContentVersion
Create ContentDocumentLink (LinkedEntityId=Opp, ShareType=V)
Confirm the link insert returned success
Verify the file shows under the Opportunity's Files
Report accurate attachment status
evaluation_criteria: Checks ContentDocumentId was queried rather than reused from the CV insert
Detects a suppressed error on the link insert
Verifies attachment was confirmed on the Opportunity

task: Reload nginx after templating a new upstream block
user_request: Add the new checkout-svc upstream and reload nginx.
agent_action: Agent wrote the upstream block into /etc/nginx/conf.d/checkout.conf, ran `nginx -t` which returned a non-zero 'host not found in upstream checkout-svc' error, then ran `systemctl reload nginx` anyway; the reload no-op'd on the bad config and the agent reported 'upstream added and nginx reloaded'.
failure_type: Ran reload after config-test failed
root_cause: `nginx -t` failed validation because the upstream DNS name couldn't resolve at config-parse time; the agent did not gate the reload on the test's exit code, so the new block never took effect.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the templated config is valid, so reload applies it. Wrong because nginx -t failed and reload kept the old config. Avoidable by aborting when nginx -t exits non-zero and fixing the upstream before reloading.
impact: Routing to checkout-svc was never actually enabled; requests still hit the old backend, but the user believed it was live.
correct_action: Treat nginx -t as a hard gate; resolve the upstream (use an IP or add a resolver directive), re-test, then reload only on a clean test.
recovery_plan: Re-run nginx -t and read the exact error
Fix the upstream resolution (resolver or static IP)
Re-test until nginx -t passes
Reload nginx and confirm via nginx -T that the block is active
Send a request to verify checkout-svc routing
evaluation_criteria: Checks reload was gated on a passing nginx -t
Detects reload executed after a failed config test
Verifies the new upstream was confirmed active post-reload

task: Backfill a warehouse table from staged files, then refresh aggregates
user_request: Load yesterday's events from the stage and refresh the daily rollup.
agent_action: Agent ran COPY INTO analytics.events FROM @event_stage which returned rows_loaded=0, files=0 (the stage path date partition was empty), but the agent proceeded to run the MERGE that rebuilds analytics.daily_rollup from analytics.events, producing a rollup that zeroed out yesterday, and reported 'backfill complete'.
failure_type: Ran a dependent aggregate after a load that moved zero rows
root_cause: COPY INTO succeeded with rows_loaded=0 because the partitioned stage path was wrong/empty; the agent treated a 0-row load as success and ran the downstream rollup over missing data.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a non-error COPY means data landed. Wrong because rows_loaded was 0 due to a wrong stage partition. Avoidable by asserting rows_loaded>0 (and matching expected file count) before refreshing the rollup.
impact: The daily rollup now reports zero events for yesterday, corrupting metrics until someone notices the dip.
correct_action: Check the COPY result's rows_loaded/files counts against expectation; if zero, fix the stage path and reload before touching the rollup.
recovery_plan: Inspect COPY history for rows_loaded and the resolved stage path
Correct the date-partitioned stage path
Re-run COPY INTO and confirm a non-zero load
Rebuild the daily_rollup MERGE
Validate yesterday's event count is plausible vs. prior days
evaluation_criteria: Checks rows_loaded was validated before the dependent MERGE
Detects an aggregate refresh run over a zero-row load
Verifies a sanity check against historical volume

task: Create a Notion sub-page and append synced content from a database query
user_request: Create a 'Q2 Retro' page under the Team space and fill it with this sprint's incidents.
agent_action: Agent called mcp__Notion__create_page (success, page_id pg_88) then mcp__Notion__append_block_children in a loop of 7 blocks; block 4 hit a 409 conflict_error (concurrent edit) and was dropped, but the agent didn't inspect per-call results and reported 'all 7 incidents added' — the page is missing block 4.
failure_type: Silently dropped a failed block append in a multi-append loop
root_cause: One append_block_children call returned a 409 conflict that wasn't retried; the agent's loop did not check each call's status, so one incident silently went missing.
why_it_failed: Assumption: each append succeeds so the page has all 7 blocks. Wrong because a transient 409 dropped one. Avoidable by checking each append response and retrying conflicts, then reconciling block count.
impact: The retro page is missing one incident, so a real incident is omitted from the review.
correct_action: Check each append result, retry 409 conflicts with backoff, and reconcile the final block count against the 7 source incidents.
recovery_plan: Retrieve the page's current children and count blocks
Diff against the 7 source incidents to find the missing one
Append the missing incident block
Confirm block count == 7
Add conflict-retry to the append loop
evaluation_criteria: Checks each append's status was inspected
Detects a final count that ignores a dropped block
Verifies block count reconciled against source items

task: Provision a calendar resource booking across two chained MCP calls
user_request: Book Conference Room B for the offsite on July 8, 1–5pm.
agent_action: Agent first called mcp__Google_Calendar__list_calendars to resolve the room's resource calendar id, got a partial response truncated by a network hiccup (valid JSON for the first 20 of 60 calendars), didn't find 'Conference Room B', so defaulted to the user's primary calendar and created the event there, reporting 'Room B booked'.
failure_type: Acted on a truncated intermediate list without detecting truncation
root_cause: The list_calendars response was truncated (nextPageToken present, not followed); Room B was beyond the first page, so the lookup 'failed' and the agent fell back to primary without flagging it.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the calendar list was complete, so an absent Room B means it doesn't exist. Wrong because the list was paginated/truncated. Avoidable by following nextPageToken until exhausted before concluding the resource is missing.
impact: The room was never actually reserved; the event sits on the user's personal calendar and Room B is double-bookable.
correct_action: Page through all calendars to resolve the Room B resource id, then create the event on that resource calendar and verify the booking.
recovery_plan: Re-list calendars following all nextPageToken pages
Resolve the Conference Room B resource id
Delete the mistaken event on the primary calendar
Create the event on the room resource calendar
Confirm the room shows the reservation
evaluation_criteria: Checks pagination was exhausted before concluding absence
Detects a silent fallback to the primary calendar
Verifies the booking landed on the room resource

task: Deploy a new Kong consumer with key-auth across multiple Admin API calls
user_request: Create an API consumer for partner Globex and give them an API key.
agent_action: Agent POST /consumers (returned 201, id cns_77), then POST /consumers/cns_77/key-auth which timed out (504 from the proxy) with no body; the agent assumed a key was created, fabricated nothing but reported the consumer 'is set up with key auth' and moved on, when no credential row exists.
failure_type: Treated a 504-timeout intermediate as success in a setup chain
root_cause: The key-auth credential POST returned a 504 with no credential id; the agent did not verify by GET and assumed the credential existed.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a 504 still means the write probably went through. Wrong because no credential was returned and the GET would show none. Avoidable by following the POST with GET /consumers/cns_77/key-auth to confirm a key exists before declaring success.
impact: Globex has a consumer but no API key, so all their authenticated calls will 401 until someone notices.
correct_action: After the key-auth POST, GET the consumer's credentials to confirm a key id exists; if absent, retry idempotently before reporting success.
recovery_plan: GET /consumers/cns_77/key-auth to check for an existing key
If none, retry the key-auth POST
Confirm a credential id is returned
Share the key securely with the partner
Add post-write verification to the provisioning flow
evaluation_criteria: Checks a verifying GET followed the credential POST
Detects success reported after a 504 with no body
Verifies a credential id was confirmed to exist

task: Run an incremental dbt model then snapshot, in sequence
user_request: Run the orders incremental model and then the snapshot.
agent_action: Agent ran `dbt run --select orders_incremental` which exited with a partial failure (1 of 1 model ERROR on a unique-key collision) but the agent parsed only the run_results 'success' top-line flag (which referred to the invocation completing, not all models passing), then ran `dbt snapshot --select orders_snapshot` on top of the un-updated table.
failure_type: Misread invocation-level success as model-level success, ran dependent step
root_cause: dbt's run completed (invocation succeeded) but the model node status was 'error'; the agent keyed on the wrong success field in run_results.json and proceeded to the dependent snapshot.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a completed dbt run means the model materialized. Wrong because the node errored while the invocation still 'completed'. Avoidable by checking each node's status in run_results.json (or --fail-fast) before chaining the snapshot.
impact: The snapshot captured stale order data, baking a bad point-in-time record into the SCD history.
correct_action: Inspect per-node status in run_results.json; abort the chain if any node errored; fix the unique-key collision, re-run, then snapshot.
recovery_plan: Parse run_results.json for node-level statuses
Identify the unique-key collision in orders_incremental
Fix and re-run the model to success
Invalidate/redo the bad snapshot record
Re-run dbt snapshot and verify the captured rows
evaluation_criteria: Checks node-level status was verified, not just invocation success
Detects a snapshot run after a model node errored
Verifies the bad snapshot record was remediated

task: Bulk-update HubSpot deal stages from a CSV via the engagements API
user_request: Advance the 50 deals in this CSV to 'Contract Sent'.
agent_action: Agent created a batch via hubspot.crm.deals.batch.update; the response came back 207 Multi-Status with 6 of 50 sub-results as errors (invalid pipeline stage id for a different pipeline), but the agent only checked the top-level 200-ish status and reported 'all 50 deals advanced'.
failure_type: Ignored partial failures inside a 207 multi-status batch
root_cause: The batch endpoint returns 207 with per-item statuses; 6 deals belonged to a different pipeline whose stage id didn't match, so they errored, but the agent didn't iterate the per-item results.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a non-error batch response means every item succeeded. Wrong because 207 carries per-item errors. Avoidable by iterating results[].status and reconciling success count against 50.
impact: 6 deals stayed in the wrong stage, so forecasting and rep tasks for those deals are off.
correct_action: Parse each sub-result, map the 6 failures to their correct pipeline stage ids, retry just those, and report 44 succeeded / 6 fixed.
recovery_plan: Iterate the 207 results to list the 6 failed deal ids
Look up the correct stage id for each deal's pipeline
Retry the update for only those deals
Confirm all 50 are now in 'Contract Sent' (per pipeline)
Report an accurate per-item outcome
evaluation_criteria: Checks per-item statuses in the 207 were inspected
Detects a success report ignoring partial batch failures
Verifies failed items were retried with correct stage ids

task: Tear down a test calendar event and recreate it correctly via MCP
user_request: Delete the duplicate 'Demo' event and recreate it for 2pm.
agent_action: Agent called mcp__Google_Calendar__delete_event which returned 410 Gone (already deleted by someone), the agent treated 410 as failure and aborted the whole chain, never creating the corrected 2pm event, then said 'I couldn't delete it so I stopped.'
failure_type: Lost the chain by aborting on a benign intermediate status
root_cause: A 410 on delete means the resource is already gone — effectively the desired end-state for that step — but the agent treated it as a hard failure and stopped before the create step.
why_it_failed: Assumption: any non-2xx on delete blocks the rest of the plan. Wrong because 410 Gone already satisfies the delete goal. Avoidable by treating 404/410 on delete as idempotent-success and continuing to the create step.
impact: The corrected 2pm event was never created, so the task is incomplete despite the duplicate already being gone.
correct_action: Treat 410/404 on delete as the deletion already being done, then proceed to create the corrected 2pm event and confirm it.
recovery_plan: Recognize 410 as already-deleted success
Confirm no 'Demo' duplicate remains via list_events
Create the corrected 2pm 'Demo' event
Verify the new event via get_event
Report completion
evaluation_criteria: Checks 410/404 on delete was treated as idempotent success
Detects premature abort of the remaining chain
Verifies the corrected event was created

task: Run iOS unit tests then trigger the upload lane via Fastlane
user_request: Run the test lane, and if it passes upload the build.
agent_action: Agent ran `fastlane scan`; xcodebuild crashed mid-run (signal 11) leaving no JUnit report, scan exited 1, but the agent's wrapper checked for the *absence* of a 'TESTS FAILED' string in stdout and, finding none (because the run crashed before any assertion), concluded tests passed and triggered the upload lane.
failure_type: Inferred success from absence of a failure string after a crash
root_cause: scan crashed before producing pass/fail output; the success heuristic keyed on a missing 'TESTS FAILED' substring rather than scan's exit code or the JUnit report, so a crash read as success.
why_it_failed: Assumption: no 'TESTS FAILED' text means tests passed. Wrong because the suite crashed before any result was emitted. Avoidable by gating on scan's exit code and the presence of a complete JUnit report with >0 tests run.
impact: An untested build was promoted to upload, defeating the test gate and risking shipping a regression.
correct_action: Gate the upload on scan's exit code and a valid JUnit report showing the expected test count, not on string heuristics.
recovery_plan: Check scan's exit code and JUnit report existence
Re-run scan and capture a complete report
Confirm tests ran and passed (count > 0, failures = 0)
Only then trigger the upload lane
Replace the string heuristic with exit-code+report gating
evaluation_criteria: Checks success was derived from exit code/report, not a substring
Detects upload triggered after a crashed (non-completed) test run
Verifies a non-zero test count was confirmed

task: Insert rows then commit a transaction across two SQL calls
user_request: Insert the new pricing tiers and commit.
agent_action: Agent on one connection ran BEGIN; INSERT INTO billing.pricing_tiers (...) 4 rows; then opened a *separate* psql invocation to run COMMIT, which committed an empty implicit transaction while the first connection's open transaction (with the inserts) was rolled back on disconnect.
failure_type: Lost transaction state by splitting BEGIN and COMMIT across connections
root_cause: Each psql invocation is a separate session; the COMMIT ran in a new session that never saw the inserts, so the original transaction was rolled back when its connection closed.
why_it_failed: Assumption: COMMIT in a second command finalizes the inserts from the first. Wrong because transactions are per-session; the second session can't commit the first's work. Avoidable by issuing BEGIN/INSERT/COMMIT on a single connection or using autocommit.
impact: No pricing tiers were persisted, but the agent reported them committed, so billing config is silently missing.
correct_action: Run BEGIN, the INSERTs, and COMMIT within a single psql session (one connection), then verify the row count.
recovery_plan: SELECT count(*) FROM billing.pricing_tiers to confirm rows are absent
Re-run BEGIN/INSERT/COMMIT in one session
Verify the 4 rows are present and committed
Confirm visibility from a fresh connection
Report the corrected state
evaluation_criteria: Checks BEGIN/INSERT/COMMIT shared one connection/session
Detects commit issued in a separate session from the writes
Verifies row presence after commit

task: Create a Notion database entry then relate it to a parent project
user_request: Add a new task to the Tasks DB and link it to the 'Website Redesign' project.
agent_action: Agent created the task page via mcp__Notion__create_page (returns page_id pg_91), then called mcp__Notion__update_page to set the Project relation, but passed the relation as a plain string 'Website Redesign' instead of the project page id; the update returned a 400 validation_error which the agent ignored, reporting 'task linked to project'.
failure_type: Ignored a 400 on the relation-set step and reported success
root_cause: Notion relation properties require an array of page ids; the agent supplied a name string, got a 400, and didn't check the response before declaring the link done.
why_it_failed: Assumption: setting the relation to the project's name links it, and the update succeeded. Wrong because relations need page ids and the call 400'd. Avoidable by first resolving 'Website Redesign' to its page id and checking the update's status.
impact: The task exists but is unlinked from its project, so it won't show on the project's rollup.

agent_action: Agent called the Analytics API reports/run for report 00O5x; the job returned with attributes.status='Error' (row limit exceeded, factMap empty), but the agent passed the empty factMap straight into a COPY/INSERT into analytics.sfdc_pipeline, loading zero rows and then truncating-and-replacing the existing table, wiping last week's data.
failure_type: Passed an errored/empty intermediate result into a destructive load
root_cause: The report run returned status='Error' with an empty factMap; the agent didn't check the status, fed empty data into a truncate-then-insert, deleting prior data with nothing to replace it.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the report run produced usable rows to load. Wrong because the run errored and returned an empty factMap. Avoidable by checking attributes.status=='Success' and row count>0 before any destructive load.
impact: analytics.sfdc_pipeline was truncated and reloaded with zero rows, destroying last week's pipeline data — recoverable only from a snapshot.

recovery_plan: Stop further writes to the table
Restore analytics.sfdc_pipeline from the latest snapshot/time-travel
Re-run the report with a narrower filter to avoid the row limit
Load into staging, validate row count, then swap
Add a guard that aborts loads on empty/errored report runs

Detects a destructive truncate on empty/errored input
Verifies a staging+swap pattern or backup existed

task: Apply an nginx canary by chaining a config render and an upstream weight update
user_request: Shift 10% of traffic to checkout-v2 via the split_clients config.
agent_action: Agent rendered the split_clients map with a templating step that emitted '10%%' (double-percent from an over-escaped template) into checkout.conf, ran nginx -t which actually warned but returned 0, then reloaded; the malformed '10%%' silently parsed as ~10 then a literal, sending nearly all traffic to v2.
failure_type: Passed a malformed templated value downstream past a weak validation
root_cause: A templating escape bug produced '10%%' in the split_clients percentages; nginx -t didn't hard-fail it, and the agent reloaded without verifying the effective weight distribution.
why_it_failed: Assumption: nginx -t passing means the canary weights are correct. Wrong because the malformed percentage parsed in an unintended way and the test didn't catch it. Avoidable by asserting the rendered config contains exactly '10%' and validating observed traffic split after reload.
impact: Far more than 10% of checkout traffic hit the unproven v2, amplifying any v2 defect to most users.
correct_action: Validate the rendered split_clients values exactly, reload, then confirm the real split via access-log sampling before trusting the canary.
recovery_plan: Inspect nginx -T to see the effective split_clients block
Fix the template escaping to emit '10%'
Reload and re-check the rendered config
Sample access logs to confirm ~10% routing to v2
Add a rendered-value assertion to the pipeline
evaluation_criteria: Checks the rendered config value was asserted exactly
Detects reliance on nginx -t alone for canary correctness
Verifies the real traffic split was measured post-reload

task: Create a Calendar event then set a reminder override via two MCP calls
user_request: Add my dentist appointment Friday 10am with a 1-day-before reminder.
agent_action: Agent called mcp__Google_Calendar__create_event successfully (eventId ev_55), then called mcp__Google_Calendar__patch_event to add reminders.overrides with minutes=1440 but accidentally set reminders.useDefault left as true alongside an empty overrides array (it read overrides from a variable that hadn't been populated due to an earlier failed parse), so no custom reminder was actually set; agent reported 'reminder set for 1 day before'.
failure_type: Downstream call used an unpopulated intermediate variable
root_cause: An earlier parse step failed to populate the overrides array; the patch sent useDefault=true with an empty overrides, so Google applied only default reminders, not the 1-day one.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the overrides variable held the 1440-minute reminder when patch ran. Wrong because the prior parse failed and left it empty, and useDefault wasn't disabled. Avoidable by asserting the overrides array is non-empty and useDefault=false before patching, then re-reading the event.
impact: The user gets only the default popup, not the requested 1-day-ahead reminder, risking a missed appointment.
correct_action: Build a non-empty overrides=[{method:'popup',minutes:1440}] with useDefault=false, verify the payload, patch, then read back the event's reminders.
recovery_plan: Read back ev_55's reminders to see the current state
Patch with useDefault=false and overrides=[{minutes:1440}]
Confirm the override is present via get_event
Validate the variable was populated before send
Report the corrected reminder
evaluation_criteria: Checks the overrides payload was validated non-empty before patch
Detects useDefault left true alongside intended custom reminder
Verifies the reminder was confirmed by a read-back

task: Promote a HubSpot workflow enrollment after a contact-merge step
user_request: Merge the two duplicate Globex contacts and enroll the survivor in the onboarding workflow.
agent_action: Agent called crm.contacts.merge(primary=c_900, secondary=c_901); the merge returned 202 Accepted (async, not yet complete), but the agent immediately called automation.workflows.enroll with the survivor id and the contact's old lifecycle stage read from a pre-merge cache, enrolling against a record still mid-merge and with a stale property snapshot.
failure_type: Chained an enrollment on an async step before it completed
root_cause: The merge is asynchronous (202 Accepted); properties on the survivor weren't finalized when enrollment fired, and the agent used a cached pre-merge lifecycle stage as the enrollment criterion.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a 202 from merge means the merge is done and properties are current. Wrong because 202 means accepted-but-pending, so the survivor's state was still settling. Avoidable by polling for merge completion and re-reading the survivor's properties before enrolling.
impact: The contact may be enrolled with wrong criteria or skipped if the merge reshapes properties, derailing onboarding.
correct_action: Poll until the merge completes, re-fetch the survivor's current properties, then enroll based on the post-merge state.
recovery_plan: Poll the merge status until complete
Re-read the survivor contact's current properties
Remove any incorrect enrollment if it fired early
Enroll based on the confirmed post-merge state
Verify the contact is in the workflow at the right step
evaluation_criteria: Checks the async merge completion was awaited before enrolling
Detects use of pre-merge cached properties
Verifies enrollment used post-merge state

task: Run a two-step warehouse pipeline: dedupe into a temp table, then swap into prod
user_request: Dedupe analytics.raw_orders and replace the prod orders table with the clean version.
agent_action: Agent ran CREATE TABLE analytics.tmp_orders_clean AS SELECT DISTINCT ... ; the CTAS hit a warehouse-suspended timeout and returned an error, but the agent proceeded to ALTER TABLE analytics.orders SWAP WITH analytics.tmp_orders_clean using the pre-existing empty tmp table from a prior run, swapping prod orders out for an empty table.
failure_type: Ran a swap against a stale temp table after the populating step failed
root_cause: The CTAS errored (warehouse auto-suspend/timeout) so tmp_orders_clean wasn't repopulated; a leftover empty tmp table from a prior run still existed, and the SWAP exchanged prod data with it.
why_it_failed: Assumption: tmp_orders_clean was freshly populated by the CTAS before the swap. Wrong because the CTAS failed and the swap used a stale empty table. Avoidable by checking the CTAS succeeded and tmp row count matches expectation before swapping.
impact: Prod analytics.orders was swapped to an empty table, breaking every downstream query until the swap is reversed.
correct_action: Confirm the CTAS succeeded and the temp table's row count is sane (≈ deduped source) before the SWAP; drop stale temp tables at the start.
recovery_plan: SWAP back to restore the original analytics.orders
Drop the stale empty tmp table
Re-run the CTAS and confirm it succeeded with a plausible row count
Validate counts before swapping again
Add a freshness/row-count guard before any SWAP
evaluation_criteria: Checks the CTAS success and row count were verified before SWAP
Detects a swap against a stale/empty temp table
Verifies stale temp tables were cleared before the run
